name: Phi-4 Mini Instruct
description:
Here is how to read the Phi-4 Mini Instruct config.json. The architecture class is Phi3ForCausalLM, which is the transformers (or equivalent) module that wires embeddings, attention, the MLP, and the language-modelling head that turns hidden states into next-token logits.

hidden_size is 3,072: that is the width of every residual stream vector. The embedding matrix is therefore 200,064 × 3,072: each token id owns a vector of that width.

num_attention_heads is 24, so each head sees 128 dimensions (3,072 / 24). The ratio test is hidden_size / num_attention_heads = 3072 / 24 = 128. 128 is a multiple of 32 (NVIDIA warp-friendly), and a multiple of 16 (Huawei cube-friendly), and a power of two (Triton / FlashAttention-friendly). From this number alone you cannot name the training chip.

num_key_value_heads is 8, so this is grouped-query attention (GQA): 24 query heads share 8 key/value groups, so the KV cache is about 3× smaller than full MHA.

num_hidden_layers is 32: the stack is that many transformer blocks deep.

intermediate_size is 8,192. In a SwiGLU MLP this is the high-dimensional workspace: the 3,072-wide stream is projected up, activated with silu, then projected back. Labs usually round this width to a multiple of 128 or 256 so it tiles on the chip.

max_position_embeddings is 131,072 tokens — the context window in the config. rope_scaling is present ({"long_factor": [1, 1.118320672, 1.250641126, 1.398617824, 1.564103225, 1.74916897, 1.956131817, 2.187582649, 2.446418898, 2.735880826, 3.059592084, 3.421605075, 3.826451687, 4.279). rope_theta is 10000.0: that is the wavelength of the rotary embedding. A larger theta keeps distant tokens from aliasing after a full rotation.

vocab_size is 200,064. 200,064 is divisible by 128. bos/eos ids, when present, are just two special rows in that table; the padded vocab is often larger than the tokenizer’s real inventory.

tie_word_embeddings is true: the same matrix is reused for input embeddings and the LM head.

torch_dtype is bfloat16. Brain floating point keeps FP32’s exponent range with less mantissa, which avoids the overflow/underflow of a tiny exponent at the cost of noisier decimals — and it halves the on-chip footprint versus FP32. NVIDIA A100s were the first NVIDIA chips with native BF16; Huawei Ascend 910-class parts also prefer BF16/FP16 on the cube.

The copy of config.json is from https://huggingface.co/microsoft/Phi-4-Mini-Instruct/blob/main/config.json.
